explanation: Fires in clauses describing a concrete physical movement, posture or bodily handling (jumped/rolled/climbed/lay/leaned/stepped/pressed/rubbed/shook/came running): it builds on the motion verb and peaks on the spatial particle or preposition right after it (onto, on, upon, into, up, over, against, beside, from) and on the following 'the'/'his'/'her'/'your' or body-part noun, regardless of whether the object noun is literal ('climbed up the rankings', 'jumped onto the bandwagon' fire as strongly). The same prepositions after abstract verbs (relied on, depends on, agreed on/upon, focuses on, based her case upon, put into effect) stay near 0, and ordinary 8-12-token abstract English (business, economics, policy, research, opinion) without any physical-motion verb stays below 0.25 x max (measured 24/24, highest 0.53 = 0.17 x max); limits: metaphorical motion verbs with a directional preposition ('stepped into the market' 0.42, 'turned her attention to' 0.54, 'looked into the' 0.39, 'fell into trouble' 0.26) can cross the line, and static location after 'is' ('The book is on the table' 0.34) fires weakly.
